title: TreeSHAP: From One Tree to a Verified Explanation

chapters.title: TreeSHAP: Start with One Small Tree
chapters.description: Start with ten dummy customers, build the tree’s predictions from their spending, and explain Maya’s $90 prediction.

chapters.title: Calculate Tree SHAP Values by Hand
chapters.description: Work through all eight feature groups and all six reveal orders, including a feature outside the prediction path.

chapters.title: How TreeSHAP Avoids Listing Every Feature Group
chapters.description: Derive leaf contributions and a polynomial dynamic program that preserves the full Shapley average.

chapters.title: When a Tree Splits on the Same Feature Twice
chapters.description: Combine repeated split conditions correctly and connect that calculation to TreeSHAP’s extend and unwind operations.

chapters.title: Choose What a Hidden Feature Means
chapters.description: Calculate path-dependent, background-replacement, and conditional explanations for the same correlated inputs.

chapters.title: From One Tree to Forests, Boosting, and Interactions
chapters.description: Combine tree explanations in the model’s output units, then read interaction matrices and global summaries.

chapters.title: Use TreeExplainer and Verify the Result
chapters.description: Run a complete random-forest example, compare two reference rules, and check the library against exhaustive masking.

chapters.title: Check a TreeSHAP Explanation Before You Trust It
chapters.description: Audit output units, reference populations, repeated features, approximations, and the conclusions an explanation supports.

sources.title: Lundberg, Erion and Lee: Consistent Individualized Feature Attribution for Tree Ensembles
